title: The five colours
summary: Each colour has a personality and its own set of abilities: the colour pie.

checklist.label: I know what the colour pie means
I know what white and blue are good at
I know what black and red are good at
I know what green is good at
I know I can mix colours

steps.title: What's the colour pie?
steps.body:
Each of Magic's five colours has a **personality**, and its own set of things it's good at. Players call this the [[color-pie|colour pie]].

The pie is why a green card can have Reach but a blue card almost never does. Once you know it, you can guess what a card does from its colour.

The pie is a design habit, not a rule. It shifts a little over the years.

visual.altText: A five-slice pie: white, blue, black, red, green.

steps.title: White {W}: order and protection
steps.body:
White values **order, community and fairness**. It wins with a team of small creatures that work together.

White is usually good at:

- Small, efficient creatures and creature tokens
- Gaining life, and [[lifelink|Lifelink]]
- [[first-strike|First strike]] and [[vigilance|Vigilance]]
- Protecting its creatures, and removing threats by exiling them

Its basic land is the Plains.

visual.altText: White's style: a team of small creatures under a sun symbol.

check.question: Which of these is a typical white ability?
check.hint: White likes to gain life and protect its team.

steps.title: Blue {U}: knowledge and control
steps.body:
Blue values **knowledge, planning and trickery**. It wins by knowing more and reacting at the right moment.

Blue is usually good at:

- [[flying|Flying]] creatures
- [[counter-spell|Countering]] spells
- Drawing extra cards
- Returning creatures to their owner's hand ("bounce")
- Tapping down an opponent's creatures

Its basic land is the Island.

visual.altText: Blue's style: a flyer and a counterspell under a water-drop symbol.

check.question: Your opponent keeps two Islands untapped and passes the turn. What might they be holding?

options.text: A counterspell, ready for your next spell
Nothing. Blue decks never keep mana open

check.hint: Countering spells is one of blue's main abilities, and it needs mana kept ready.

steps.title: Black {B}: power at any price
steps.body:
Black values **power and ambition**, and will pay any price for them, including its own life and creatures.

Black is usually good at:

- Destroying creatures
- Making opponents discard cards
- [[deathtouch|Deathtouch]]
- Draining life: opponents lose it, black gains it
- Bringing creatures back from the graveyard

Its basic land is the Swamp.

visual.altText: Black's style: removal and a creature returning from the graveyard, under a skull symbol.

steps.title: Red {R}: speed and fire
steps.body:
Red values **freedom, emotion and action**. It wants to win fast, before the opponent gets set up.

Red is usually good at:

- [[haste|Haste]] creatures that attack right away
- Direct damage to creatures or players ("burn")
- Destroying artifacts
- Taking control of a creature until end of turn

Its basic land is the Mountain.

visual.altText: Red's style: a charging creature and a burn spell under a flame symbol.

check.question: A creature can attack the same turn it's cast. Which colour is this most typical of?
check.hint: Think of the keyword Haste, and which colour wants to win fast.

steps.title: Green {G}: growth and nature
steps.body:
Green values **nature, growth and strength**. It wins by growing bigger than everyone else.

Green is usually good at:

- The biggest creatures, often with [[trample|Trample]]
- [[reach|Reach]], so its creatures can block flyers
- Making extra mana early ("ramp")
- Destroying artifacts and enchantments
- Letting its creatures fight each other's

Its basic land is the Forest.

visual.altText: Green's style: a big creature and extra mana under a tree symbol.

check.question: An opponent's creature has Flying. Which green ability lets your creature block it?
check.hint: Look at the second point in the list.

steps.title: Mixing colours
steps.body:
You can build a deck with **any colours you like**. Each colour needs its own lands, so one or two colours is easiest at first.

On the pie, each colour sits between two **allies** that share its values, and across from two **enemies** that pull the other way. Green and red are allies; green and blue are enemies.

Picking a colour is a bit like picking a personality. Which one sounds like you?

visual.altText: The colour pie with ally and enemy lines drawn.

check.question: Can a deck use more than one colour?

options.text: Yes, but each colour needs its own lands
No, decks are always one colour

check.hint: Look at the first sentence of this step.
